To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light scatter properties of a cell/suspended solid mixture are essentially linear in the cell concentration, that there exist wavelength intervals in which the light is independent of the concentration of the suspended solids and only a function on cell concentration, and that these wavelength intervals can be used to determine cell concentration in the mixture.

the light scatter spectrum from cell/solid substrate mixture has invariant regions in which the light scattering intensity is a linear function of the cell concentration, and that the invariant region can be used to quantify the cell concentration.
light scatter from cells in the presence suspended solids can be used to estimate cell concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a novel light scatter sensor to estimate the cell concentrations in the presence of solids.
the development of a novel sensor for the measurement of cell concentration in fermentation processes.
the development of an instrument for measuring cell concentrations in the presence of solids and with the theoretical understanding of the underlying physical processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cell concentration can be estimated in the presence of a suspended solids background by using light scatter measurements in the wavelength range 500 to 800 nm, with the wavelength of the light scatter measurement being selected to fall within one of the invariant regions.
light scatter from cell suspensions in the presence of solids is a linear function of the concentration of the cells and is independent of the solid substrate concentration.
light scatter is a useful and reliable method to estimate cell concentration in the absence of suspended solids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light scatter technique is a viable method for estimating cell concentration in the process streams of bioprocesses.
the cell concentration can be estimated from light scatter data, provided that the light scatter data is collected at wavelengths corresponding to the invariant regions.
we developed a novel sensor based on light scatter to measure the concentration of cells in the fermentation broth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light scatter spectrum from cells can be used as a tool to estimate cell concentration.
light scatter from cells and light scatter from solids are independent of each other.
the light scatter spectrum from cell/suspended solids mixtures is a function of cell and suspended solid concentrations.
